quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are allowed to use the full width of a lane. Make sure your car is completely in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Only know the general direction of your destination.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you leave. Do not start with only a vague idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map before you drive.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far your vehicle takes to stop?
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. This changes based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers to be careful when the road is wet because the pavement is slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while you are driving, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep your car straight. Slow down gradually by lifting your foot off the gas pedal and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands must be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely on highways.

questions.question: If someone is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually to encourage them to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake suddenly, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually to encourage them to pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to drive around you.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming toward you from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a rural area, unless federal law allows a higher speed?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in rural areas is 55 mph, unless federal law allows higher. In cities and residential areas, the maximum is 30 mph.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Check both tracks before crossing. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.explanation: When hit from behind, keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and resting your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection. You have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. This keeps your vehicle from rolling into traffic. On a street without a curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze faster than regular roads because they are suspended in the air. Drive carefully when crossing bridges in freezing weather.

questions.question: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should set the parking brake and turn your wheels:
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb toward the center of the street. The back of the front tire will touch the curb.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: After checking traffic and signaling, stop parallel to the car directly ahead of your parking space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: You should signal 50 to 75 feet before turning at an intersection.
questions.explanation: South Carolina law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before making any turn.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and can expect oncoming traffic to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is about to appear. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill or downgrade is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a dangerous downgrade or hill ahead. The hill may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid out of control, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering to regain control until the car is moving safely again.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What color are lane markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Is a driver license a right or a privilege?
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege you must earn and keep. It is not a right.

questions.question: While waiting in an intersection to turn left, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask for space.
Drive around the back of a blocked car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. This protects you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the road edge when parking uphill with no curb. This keeps the car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: How can you avoid headlight glare from an oncoming car?

options.text: Look briefly to the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright glare. Then look ahead again to check the other car's position.
